cases.r_call: local({ x <- airquality$Ozone; n <- length(x); s <- log(mean(x)) - mean(log(x)); k <- uniroot(function(k) log(k) - digamma(k) - s, c(0.1, 10), tol = 1e-15)$root; b <- k / mean(x); list(standard_errors = sqrt(diag(solve(n * matrix(c(trigamma(k), -1 / b, -1 / b, k / b^2), 2))))) })
cases.tolerance_reason: R evaluates the exact Fisher information of the gamma law at the MLE; probstat inverts a central-difference Hessian of the log-likelihood, accurate to about 2e-7 relative.
cases.note: fitdistrplus's standard errors come from optim's Hessian (finite differences with ndeps = 1e-3) and are 1.2e-3 relative from the exact values, so the exact information is the reference.

cases.r_call: local({ f <- fitdist(airquality$Ozone, "weibull", method = "mle", control = list(reltol = 1e-15, maxit = 10000)); list(estimates = f$estimate, log_likelihood = f$loglik) })
cases.tolerance_reason: fitdistrplus maximizes by Nelder-Mead (reltol 1e-15), which stops about 4e-8 relative from the root of the likelihood equations; probstat solves those equations.

cases.r_call: local({ x <- airquality$Ozone; b <- uniroot(function(b) sum(x^b * log(x)) / sum(x^b) - 1 / b - mean(log(x)), c(0.5, 5), tol = 1e-15)$root; list(estimates = c(b, mean(x^b)^(1 / b))) })
cases.tolerance_reason: Both sides solve the Weibull profile equation for the shape to full precision; the scale follows in closed form.

cases.r_call: local({ f <- fitdist(airquality$Ozone, "lnorm", method = "mle"); list(estimates = f$estimate, log_likelihood = f$loglik) })
cases.tolerance_reason: fitdistrplus and probstat both use the closed-form log-normal MLE.

cases.r_call: local({ y <- log(airquality$Ozone); n <- length(y); s <- sqrt(mean((y - mean(y))^2)); list(standard_errors = c(s / sqrt(n), s / sqrt(2 * n))) })
cases.tolerance_reason: R evaluates the exact inverse Fisher information; probstat inverts a central-difference Hessian of the log-likelihood, accurate to about 3e-8 relative.
Both sides evaluate the same closed form; only floating-point rounding differs.
cases.note: fitdistrplus matches the mean and the biased (divisor n) variance, as probstat does.

cases.r_call: local({ g <- ismev::gev.fit(portpirie, show = FALSE, method = "Nelder-Mead", maxit = 100000, reltol = 1e-15); list(estimates = g$mle, log_likelihood = -g$nllh) })
cases.tolerance_reason: ismev maximizes by Nelder-Mead (reltol 1e-15); the simplex stops on function values, which leaves the parameters free by about 1e-7 relative.
cases.note: ismev and probstat share the sign convention: xi > 0 is the heavy-tailed Frechet type.

skipped.reason: probstat's simple and Holt exponential smoothing concentrate the initial level and trend out by least squares, while HoltWinters starts from the first observations (l.start = x[1], or x[2] and x[2] - x[1]); the fitted smoothing parameters and SSE differ by construction.
probstat implements only the moment ratios g1 and g2 (e1071 type 1); the bias-adjusted G1/G2 (type 2) and b1/b2 (type 3) have no probstat function.
probstat reports the sample odds ratio ad/bc rather than R's conditional maximum-likelihood estimate; the p-values are compared.

skipped.r_function: fisher.test on r x c tables
skipped.reason: probstat's fisher_exact_test is defined for 2 x 2 tables only.
probstat has no Welch one-way ANOVA.

probstat's additive models use Eilers-Marx P-splines with their own knot placement and identifiability constraint; mgcv's default thin-plate regression splines (and its bs = "ps" variant with different knot conventions) do not define the same penalized fit.
lme4 is not installed; nlme::lme is used for the REML comparison.
car is not installed; the base-R ANOVA of absolute deviations is used instead.

summary.rlm scales sqrt(sum(psi^2) / (n - p)) by Huber's correction factor kappa / mean(psi') and uses (X'WX)^-1; probstat reports the sandwich s^2 n / (n - p) A^-1 B A^-1, so only coefficients and scale are compared.
probstat.statistics.quantile implements Hyndman-Fan types 1 and 7 only; both are compared.

fitdist inverts optim's finite-difference Hessian (ndeps = 1e-3), 1.2e-3 relative from the exact gamma information on airquality$Ozone; the exact Fisher information evaluated in base R is the reference instead.

gev.fit inverts optim's finite-difference Hessian (ndeps = 1e-3); on portpirie its standard errors differ from probstat's central-difference observed information by 4e-6, 1.2e-4, and 2.8e-5 relative (mu, sigma, xi), and base R offers no exact GEV information to arbitrate.
R's default constant 1.4826 is rounded; the case passes constant = 1 / qnorm(0.75), probstat's constant.
